questions.stem: Choose the correct options from the given statements of the enteric nervous system?Vagus is the only afferent from gutFunctions independent of brain and Spinal cordMyenteric plexus in the lamina propriaExclusively under the influence of nervesParasympathetic connects enteric to CNSSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
2
  • Among the given options, the correct statement is that the enteric nervous system functions independent of the brain and spinal cord and this is the reason it is called the mini brain of the gut.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 789

questions.stem: LMN lesions are associated with?Decrease in muscle toneSpastic paralysisBabinski positiveFasciculationsSelect the correct answer from the given below code:

questions.stem: Which of these systems do not require ATP?ParacellularSimple diffusionFacilitated diffusionAntiport (Na/K ATPase)SymportSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1,2,3
  • Paracellular transport, simple diffusion, facilitated diffusion are examples of passive transport and ATP is not required in these processes

questions.stem: Which of the following is not seen in decompression sickness?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hemodilution
  • Of the options given, hemodilution is not seen in decompression sickness, whereas hemoconcentration is seen ( due to extravasation of plasma, as a result of capillary leak).


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.564

questions.stem: Which receptor contributes to static 2 point discrimination?

questions.stemHtml: The O₂ saturation with respect to PO₂ is marked as A. What happens to the Oxygen Hb dissociation curve upon transfusion of stored RBC?
questions.solutionHtml:
B
  • In stored blood, 2,3-DPG concentration decreases and on transfusion they decrease the oxygen transport resulting in left shift ( curve B)
  • The effect is less when blood is stored in acid citrate dextrose solution


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 526

questions.stem: Peripheral chemoreceptors are most sensitive to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hypoxia
  • Peripheral chemoreceptors respond to changes in PO2 , PCO2 and pH in arterial blood
  • The major stimulus for activation is reduced PO2 ( hypoxia )


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition , Page No. 535

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about Physiological dead space?

options.label: B
options.text: Is lesser than anatomical dead space

questions.solutionHtml:
Represents inadequately perfused alveoli
  • Physiological dead space represents inadequately perfused alveoli and not inadequately ventilated alveoli


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 498,Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.1442
